lesson.grammar_point: relative clauses with who, that and where

listenings.text: Welcome to the neighborhood walk. Before we start, three places that people always ask about. The first one is the small boutique on the corner, the one with the green door. That is the shop that sells clothes from local designers only, and nothing in it costs more than a dinner for two. The second one is the old cinema across the street. It is now a library, but it is still the place where everybody meets before a night out, because nobody can miss it. It is the only real landmark we have. And the third one is not a place, it is a person. Ask for Mr. Costa. He is the tailor who fixed half of the jackets in this city, and he has worked in the same room for forty years. If you have something that does not fit, he is the man who can save it.

When I moved to a new city for university, the person who helped me most was not a teacher. It was my roommate, a girl who was in her third year and knew everything. She showed me the cafe where students study after nine at night, because the library closes early. She showed me the market that sells fabric by the meter, and that is where I bought everything for my first project. And she introduced me to a woman who became my mentor, a designer who was looking for somebody to help her two afternoons a week. I did not ask for any of that. My roommate just kept saying, you need to meet the person who, you need to see the place where. I still have the souvenir she gave me on my last day: a small key ring from the cafe. I keep it on my bag.
